start.description: Start timestamp for the value.  If null, assumed to be beginning-of-time (BOT).

end.description: End timestamp for the value.  If null, assumed to be end-of-time (EOT).

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

expectedSensor.description:
Matched sensor in {@link FailureModeLibrary} for this asset-sensor pair. Sensors may be
associated with different expected sensors when being considered in the context of different
assets, e.g. a sensor which acts as OUTLET_PRESSURE for one asset could be INLET_PRESSURE
for a different asset.

reconstructionHeaderName.description: Header name for the reconstruction series associated with this asset-sensor pair.

title:
Clusters a {@link Sensor} together with a {@link ReliabilityAsset} for ML modeling purposes.
Represents a conceptual relation. Physical/hierarchical relations are represented with the {@link ReliabilityAssetSensorHierarchicalRelation} type.

**Note**: Since this type mixes {@link TimedIntervalRelation}, it is important to specify an {@link id} when
attempting to create a new instance if you want to guarantee a new instance is actually created. Otherwise, if you
attempt to create a new instance with the same {@link from} as an existing instance, it may just be merged into the
existing instance.

For additional usage documentation, look to {@link Sensor} and the reliability dev guide topic titled
"Tags and Sensors".
name: ReliabilityAssetSensorRelation
